forum.title: Interface to 24V encoder via optocoupler
forum.best_answer_content:
Hello,

My standpoint: it is recommended to use an optocoupler to protect STM32 microcontroller from high-voltage spikes and ground loops in your case and you need to use a high-speed optocoupler. Example [6N137](https://www.vishay.com/docs/84732/6n137.pdf). (I think it can handle up to 5MHz as input. You need to contact its manufacturer Vishay).

You need to limit the current on the LED side from 24V. Example: if you use 6N137 as an optocoupler, to limit the current on the LED, you need to add a resistor in series Where ***R = (Vencoder - VF LED) / IF LED*** .

* Vencoder = 24V

* VF LED = 1.4V (see a screenshot from the optocoupler datasheet below)

* IF LED = 10mA (see a screenshot from the optocoupler datasheet below)

![screenshot1.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/b005d4f6-b91a-135e-463d-f3bbd3cfeaab.png "screenshot1.png")

R = 2,260K. Standard value: 2.2K.

Hope I've answered your question.
forum.content_text:
*Split from: [Evaluation of Encoder Signal Level Shifting Approach](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-products/evaluation-of-encoder-signal-level-shifting-approach/td-p/732158) as that was a different issue, and has been solved.*

---

I am also working with this same issue, in my case i have a encoder operating at 24V, and signal in comparable frequency

i have implemented a simple voltage divider, the circuit works just fine, but as i don't have equipment to measure the noise and also i would prefer to have galvanic separation to my MCU, so in this case is there any good suggested  level shifter or optocoupler, should i combine the both strategy of voltage divider and optocoupler or just 1 is fine (from perspective of noise and safety)?
